macros.name: doendnotes
macros.doc: \doendnotes is the command you use to print one series of endnotes; it takes one argument: the series letter of the note series you want to print.

macros.name: edaftertab
macros.doc: \edaftertab{⟨entry⟩}{⟨text⟩}, where ⟨entry⟩ is an entry in the rightmost column, typesets ⟨text⟩ right justified after the ⟨entry⟩.

macros.name: edatleft
macros.doc: \edatleft[⟨math⟩]{⟨symbol⟩}{⟨halfheight⟩} typesets the math ⟨symbol⟩ as \left<symbol> with the optional ⟨math⟩ centered before it.

macros.name: edatleft

macros.name: edbeforetab
macros.doc: \edbeforetab{⟨text⟩}{⟨entry⟩}, where ⟨entry⟩ is an entry in the leftmost column, typesets ⟨text⟩ left justified before the ⟨entry⟩.

macros.name: edindex
macros.doc: The \edindex{⟨item⟩} macro can be used in numbered text to specify that ⟨item⟩ and the current page & linenumber should be added to the raw index file.

macros.name: edindex

macros.name: edlabel
macros.doc: The \edlabel command works by writing macros to LaTeX.aux file.

macros.name: edpageref
macros.doc: If the specified label exists, \edpageref gives its page number.

macros.name: edrowfill
macros.doc: The macro \edrowfill{⟨start⟩}{⟨end⟩}{⟨fill⟩} fills columns number ⟨start⟩ to ⟨end⟩ inclusive with ⟨fill⟩.

macros.name: edtabcolsep
macros.doc: The distance between the columns is controlled by the length \edtabcolsep.

macros.name: edtext
macros.doc: The ⟨lemma⟩ argument is the lemma in the main text: \edtext both prints this as part of the text, and makes it available to the ⟨commands⟩ you specify to generate notes.

macros.name: edvertdots
macros.doc: The \edvertdots macro is similar to \edvertline except that it produces a vertical dotted instead of a solid line.

macros.name: edvertline
macros.doc: The macro \edvertline{⟨height⟩} draws a vertical line ⟨height⟩ high (contrast this with \edatright where the size argument is half the desired height).

macros.name: endashchar
macros.doc: The \endashchar macro is simply an en-dash from the normal font and is immune to changes in the surrounding font.

macros.name: endlock
macros.doc: You can use \startlock or \endlock in running text to start or end line number locking at the current line.

macros.name: endnumbering
macros.doc: \endnumbering closes the ⟨jobname⟩.nn file.

macros.name: endstanzaextra
macros.doc: The macro \endstanzaextra, if it is defined, is called at the end of a stanza.

macros.name: endsub
macros.doc: \startsub and \endsub turn sub-lineation on and off, by writing appropriate instructions to the line-list file.

macros.name: extensionchars
macros.doc: When the package assembles the name of the auxiliary file for a section, it prefixes \extensionchars to the section number.

macros.name: firstlinenum
macros.doc: \firstlinenum specifies the first line that will have a printed number, and \linenumincrement is the difference between succesive numbered lines.

macros.name: flagstanza
macros.doc: Putting \flagstanza[⟨len⟩]{⟨text⟩} at the start of a line in a stanza (or elsewhere) will typeset ⟨text⟩ at a distance ⟨len⟩ before the line.

macros.name: flagstanza
macros.doc: Putting \flagstanza[⟨len⟩]{⟨text⟩} at the start of a line in a stanza (or elsewhere) will typeset ⟨text⟩ at a distance ⟨len⟩ before the line.

macros.name: fnpos
macros.doc: The \fnpos and \mpfnpos simply place their arguments in \@fnpos and \@mpfnpos, which will be used later in the output routine.

macros.name: footfootmarkA
macros.doc: The command \footfootmarkA controls the appearance of the mark at the start of the footnote text.

macros.name: footnormalX
macros.doc: \footnormalX{⟨series⟩} initialises the settings for the ⟨series⟩ footnotes.

macros.name: footparagraph
macros.doc: The \footparagraph macro sets up everything for one series of the footnotes so that they’ll be paragraphed; it takes the series letter as argument.

macros.name: footthreecol
macros.doc: You say \footthreecol{A} to have the A series of the footnotes typeset in three columns.

macros.name: foottwocol
macros.doc: You say \foottwocol{A} to have the A series of the footnotes typeset in two columns.

macros.name: fullstop
macros.doc: \endashchar and \fullstop, which produce an en-dash and a full stop respectively from the normal document font, whatever font you are using for the numbers.

macros.name: hangingsymbol
macros.doc: The macro \hangingsymbol is used to insert a symbol on each hanging of verses.

macros.name: hidenumbering
macros.doc: When inserted into a numbered line the macro \hidenumbering causes the number for that particular line to be hidden; namely, no line number will print.

macros.name: hsizethreecol
macros.doc: \hsizethreecol[⟨s⟩]{⟨l⟩} is used to change width of a column when critical notes are displaying in three columns.

macros.doc: \hsizetwocol[⟨s⟩]{⟨l⟩} is used to change width of a column when critical notes are displaying in two columns.

macros.name: inplaceoflemmaseparator

macros.name: inplaceofnumber

macros.name: labelpstarttrue
macros.doc: With the \labelpstarttrue command, a \label added just after a \pstart will refer to the number of this pstart.

macros.name: ledinnernote
macros.doc: \ledinnernote{⟨text⟩} will put ⟨text⟩ into the inner margin level with where the command was issued.

macros.name: ledlsnotesep
macros.doc: The texts are put a distance \ledlsnotesep (or \ledrsnotesep) into the left (or right) margin.

macros.name: ledlsnotewidth
macros.doc: The left sidenote text is put into a box of width \ledlsnotewidth and the right text into a box of width \ledrsnotewidth.

macros.name: ledouternote
macros.doc: \ledouternote{⟨text⟩} puts ⟨text⟩ in the outer margin.

macros.name: ledrightnote
macros.doc: \ledleftnote, \ledrightnote, \ledinnernote, \ledouternote are the user commands for left, right, inner and outer sidenotes.

macros.name: ledrsnotesep
macros.doc: The texts are put a distance \ledlsnotesep (or \ledrsnotesep) into the left (or right) margin.

macros.name: ledrsnotewidth
macros.doc: The left sidenote text is put into a box of width \ledlsnotewidth and the right text into a box of width \ledrsnotewidth.

macros.name: ledsidenote
macros.doc: \ledsidenote{⟨text⟩} will put ⟨text⟩ into the margin specified by the current setting of \sidenotemargin{⟨location⟩}.

macros.name: leftlinenum
macros.doc: \leftlinenum and \rightlinenum are the macros that are called to print marginal line numbers on a page, for left- and right-hand margins respectively.

macros.name: leftnoteupfalse
macros.doc: If you want they to be placed to align with the first line of the note to which it refers, use \leftnoteupfalse (for left note) and/or \rightnoteupfalse (for right note).

macros.name: lemma
macros.doc: If you want to change the lemma that gets passed to the notes, you can do this by using \lemma{⟨alternative⟩} within the second argument to \edtext, before the note commands.

macros.name: lineation
macros.doc: Lines can be numbered either by page, by pstart or by section; you specify this using the \lineation{⟨arg⟩} macro, where ⟨arg⟩ is either page, pstart or section.

macros.name: linenum
macros.doc: You can use \linenum{⟨arg⟩} to change the line numbers passed to the notes.

macros.name: linenumberlist
macros.doc: You can define \linenumberlist to specify a non-uniform distribution of printed line numbers.

macros.name: linenumberstyle
macros.doc: You can use \linenumberstyle{⟨style⟩} to change the numbering style.

macros.name: linenumincrement
macros.doc: \firstlinenum specifies the first line that will have a printed number, and \linenumincrement is the difference between succesive numbered lines.

macros.name: linenummargin
macros.doc: The command \linenummargin⟨location⟩ specifies the margin where the line (or pstart) numbers will be printed.

macros.name: linenumsep
macros.doc: You’ll generally want a kern between a line number and the text, and \linenumsep is provided as a standard way of storing its size.

macros.name: lockdisp
macros.doc: When line locking is being used, the \lockdisp{⟨word⟩} macro specifies whether a line number—if one is due to appear—should be printed on the first printed line or on the last, or by all of them.

macros.name: morenoexpands
macros.doc: You can define the macro \morenoexpands to modify macros that you call within \edtext.

macros.name: mpfnpos
macros.doc: The \fnpos and \mpfnpos simply place their arguments in \@fnpos and \@mpfnpos, which will be used later in the output routine.

macros.name: multfootsep
macros.doc: \multfootsep is used as the separator between footnote markers.

macros.name: newseries
macros.doc: If you need more than six series of critical footnotes you can create extra series, using \newseries command.

macros.name: nolemmaseparator
macros.doc: You can suppress the lemma separator, using \nolemmaseparator[⟨s⟩], which is simply a alias of \lemmaseparator[⟨s⟩]{}.

macros.name: nolemmaseparator
macros.doc: You can suppress the lemma separator, using \nolemmaseparator[⟨s⟩], which is simply a alias of \lemmaseparator[⟨s⟩]{}.

macros.name: nonumberinfootnote

macros.name: nonumberinfootnote

macros.name: notefontsizeX

macros.doc: \notefontsizeX[⟨s⟩]{⟨command⟩} is used to define the font size of critical footnotes of the series.

macros.name: notenumfontX
macros.doc: \notenumfontX[⟨s⟩]{⟨command⟩} is used to change the font style for note numbers in familiar footnotes.

macros.name: notenumfontX
macros.doc: \notenumfontX[⟨s⟩]{⟨command⟩} is used to change the font style for note numbers in familiar footnotes.

macros.name: numberlinefalse
macros.doc: Line numbering can be disabled with \numberlinefalse.

macros.name: numberpstartfalse
macros.doc: You can stop the numbering with \numberpstartfalse.

macros.name: numlabfont
macros.doc: Line numbers are usually printed in a smaller font, and \numlabfont is provided as a standard name for that font.

macros.name: onlypstartinfootnote
macros.doc: In combination with \pstartinfootnote, you can use \onlypstartinfootnote[⟨s⟩] if you want to print only the pstart number in the footnote, and not the line and subline number.

macros.name: onlypstartinfootnote
macros.doc: In combination with \pstartinfootnote, you can use \onlypstartinfootnote[⟨s⟩] if you want to print only the pstart number in the footnote, and not the line and subline number.

macros.name: pagelinesep
macros.doc: The page & linenumber combination is written as page\pagelinesep line, where the default definition is \newcommand{\pagelinesep}{-} so that an item on page 3, line 5 will be noted as being at 3-5.

macros.name: parafootsep
macros.doc: For paragraphed footnotes (see below), you can choose the separator between each note by using \parafootsep[⟨s⟩]{⟨text⟩}.

macros.name: parafootsep
macros.doc: For paragraphed footnotes (see below), you can choose the separator between each note by using \parafootsep[⟨s⟩]{⟨text⟩}.

macros.name: parindentX
macros.doc: Use \parindentX[⟨series⟩] to enable indentation.

macros.name: parindentX
macros.doc: Use \parindentX[⟨series⟩] to enable indentation.

macros.name: pstartinfootnote
macros.doc: You can use \pstartinfootnote[⟨s⟩] if you want to print the pstart number in the footnote, before the line and subline number.

macros.name: pstartinfootnote
macros.doc: You can use \pstartinfootnote[⟨s⟩] if you want to print the pstart number in the footnote, before the line and subline number.

macros.name: pstartref
macros.doc: If the specified label exists, \pstartref gives its pstart number.

macros.name: raggedX
macros.doc: Text in paragraphed footnotes is justified, but you can use \raggedX[⟨s⟩]+L+ if you want it to be ragged left, or \raggedX[⟨s⟩]+R if you want it to be ragged right.

macros.name: raggedX
macros.doc: Text in paragraphed footnotes is justified, but you can use \raggedX[⟨s⟩]+L+ if you want it to be ragged left, or \raggedX[⟨s⟩]+R if you want it to be ragged right.

macros.name: rightlinenum
macros.doc: \leftlinenum and \rightlinenum are the macros that are called to print marginal line numbers on a page, for left- and right-hand margins respectively.

macros.name: seriesatbegin
macros.doc: \seriesatbegin{⟨s⟩} changes the order of series, to put the series ⟨s⟩ at the beginning of the list.

macros.name: seriesatend
macros.doc: \seriesatend moves the series to the end of the list.

macros.name: setline
macros.doc: The \setline{⟨num⟩} and \advanceline{⟨num⟩} commands may be used to change the current line’s number (or the sub-line number, if sub-lineation is currently on).

macros.name: setlinenum
macros.doc: You can use \setlinenum{⟨num⟩} before a \pstart to set the visible line-number to a specified positive value.

macros.name: showlemma
macros.doc: \showlemma{⟨lemma⟩} typesets the lemma text in the body.

macros.name: sidenotesep
macros.doc: This macro is used to separate sidenotes of the same line.

macros.name: skipnumbering
macros.doc: When inserted into a numbered line the macro \skipnumbering causes the numbering of that particular line to be skipped; that is, the line number is unchanged and no line number will be printed.

macros.name: spreadmath
macros.doc: \spreadmath{⟨math⟩} typesets {⟨math⟩} but the {⟨math⟩} has no effect on the calculation of column widths.

macros.name: stanza
macros.doc: Use \stanza at the start of a stanza.

macros.name: stanza
macros.doc: Use \stanza at the start of a stanza.

macros.name: stanzaindent
macros.doc: You can set the indent of some specific verse by calling \stanzaindent{⟨value⟩} at the beginning of the verse, before any other character.

macros.name: stanzaindent*
macros.doc: You can set the indent of some specific verse by calling \stanzaindent{⟨value⟩} at the beginning of the verse, before any other character.

macros.name: stanzaindentbase
macros.doc: The indents are integer multiples of the length \stanzaindentbase, whose default value is 20pt.

macros.name: startlock
macros.doc: The \startlock command, used in running text, locks the line number at its current value, until you say \endlock.

macros.name: startstanzahook
macros.doc: the macro \startstanzahook is called at the beginning of a stanza.

macros.name: startsub
macros.doc: You insert the \startsub and \endsub commands in your text to turn sublineation on and off.

macros.name: sublinenumberstyle
macros.doc: \sublinenumberstyle{⟨style⟩} can be used to change the numbering style of sub-line numbers, which is normally arabic numerals.

macros.name: sublineref
macros.doc: If the specified label exists, \sublineref gives its sub-line number.

macros.name: symlinenum

macros.name: symlinenum

macros.name: twolines
macros.doc: The ⟨text⟩ argument of \twolines will be printed if the lemma is on two lines, and the ⟨text⟩ argument of \morethantwolines will be printed if the lemma is on three or more lines.

macros.name: twolines

macros.name: txtbeforeXnotes
